summary: Throttle smoothing mismatch and healthcheck sampling counted against tenant tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports a sudden increase in 429 responses during normal traffic after enabling a short smoothing window on the dedicated pool rate limiter. They observe tenant token depletion spikes that align with healthcheck probes from their internal orchestrator.

Impact:
- Multiple realtime endpoints returning 429s for ~2–3 minute bursts every 15 minutes, affecting checkout personalization and search ranking features.
- Customer reports ~8% error rate for low-latency routes during bursts, increasing e2e latency and causing retries in their service.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightCart lease id: lease-91b7) in prod/us-east.
- Rate limiter config rolled out yesterday: smoothing_window=10s (reduced from 60s), healthcheck sampling enabled on route /_hc, priority routing enabled for low-latency lane.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use a small fleet of workers (16) to send steady interactive traffic (~12 rps) to /v1/chat with pinned model redwood-open-7b.
2) Run a healthcheck loop that pings /_hc every 30s from a separate monitoring agent (3 probes concurrently).
3) Observe 429 spikes on interactive endpoints when the healthcheck cluster performs concurrent probes and when smoothing window is short.

Observed behavior:
- Healthcheck requests appear to be counted toward tenant token bucket immediately and trigger short, intense token consumption peaks.
- Smoothing window reduction causes refill accounting to be more granular, exposing short bursts rather than smoothing them out.

Expected behavior:
- Healthcheck traffic should be accounted in a way that does not amplify microbursts for interactive lanes (either sub-sampled or mapped to a separate background pool).
- Short smoothing windows should not cause periodic ~2–3 minute tenant-wide 429 waves for typical monitoring patterns.

Workaround so far:
- Customer temporarily disabled healthcheck sampling and reverted smoothing_window to 60s which reduced 429 frequency.

Additional context:
- Customer provided request IDs and timestamps (attached). They noted the bursts always correlate with their monitoring agent schedule.
- BrightCart is on a dedicated contract and requests guidance for a conservative default and an explicit option to exclude internal health probes from the interactive quota.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Short smoothing window reduces the effective refill blur so small periodic probes appear as sharp token drains at refill boundaries.
Hypothesis 2: Healthcheck requests are treated as interactive by default and counted against the same token bucket as user requests; concurrent probes multiply apparent concurrency.
Data: Token refill logs (token-service) show refill intervals at 10s after config change; token consumption graph attached in PR #214 shows spike alignment with probe timestamps.
Staging tests: Sub-sampling healthcheck requests (1 in 3 accepted) in staging reduced peak token draw by ~68% and eliminated the tenant-wide 429 wave in our 4-hour run.
Edge case: If customer uses many monitoring agents across multiple IP pools, sub-sampling alone may not be enough; recommend mapping healthchecks to a background/burst pool.
Related runbooks: See Rate Limiter Design and Priority Pools (confluence link) for background-pool mapping and dedicated-pool config knobs.
resolution: Implemented route-level pool mapping toggle and healthcheck sub-sampling option for dedicated pools. Ran canary on BrightCart lease-91b7; reverted smoothing_window back to 10s without reintroducing 429 spikes when healthcheck mapping is enabled.
resolution_notes: Change delivered via infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321 (rate-limiter: add route.pool_override and healthcheck.subsample_rate).
Canary window: 2026-03-12 02:00–04:00 UTC on lease-91b7. Metrics: 429 rate dropped from 8% bursts to <0.2% and average latency stable.
Workaround documented: Console toggle for dedicated customers to map /_hc to background pool and set healthcheck.subsample_rate default to 0.33.
Follow-up action: Product to add UI exposure for route pool mapping and support docs update (ticket created: INT-2026-docs-for-pool-mapping).
Customer confirmation: BrightCart support (Elena Rojas) confirmed post-canary behavior acceptable and requested permanent opt-in.
